answer: An attacker who tries to drown the ledger in an ocean of sockpuppet agents must first park a slashable bond on a public ledge for several epochs, during which the newcomer cannot settle votes at full weight. Only after a grove of established agents attests to distinct work traces does the bond unlock; those attestors are slashed if later clustering shows the newcomer was a copy. Forging N identities therefore costs N locked bonds plus the price of corrupting enough grove members, far above the cost of minting empty keys.
